config.title: Build a typeahead autocomplete box

intro.title: Build a typeahead autocomplete box
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typeahead autocomplete box—a search input that suggests matching options as the user types. You'll learn how to filter an array of data based on user input to display real-time suggestions. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, string methods, and DOM event handling for input changes. This project will help you understand dynamic UI updates and basic search functionality in a web application.
intro.usecase: Typeahead autocomplete is essential for modern user interfaces where quick search and data entry are required. You'll find this pattern in e-commerce search bars that suggest products as you type, form fields that auto-complete addresses or email addresses, and dashboard filters that help users narrow down large datasets. As a developer, implementing this feature improves user experience by reducing typing effort, preventing input errors, and helping users discover available options faster. This skill is valuable for building responsive search interfaces, smart form components, and interactive data exploration tools.

objectives: Construct a basic HTML structure for the typeahead input and results container
Initialize and manage the state for user input and filtered suggestions
Implement an event handler to capture and process user keystrokes
Apply a filtering algorithm to match input against a dataset of suggestions
Render dynamic search results that update based on the current input
Bind keyboard navigation events to allow selection of suggestions
Control the visibility of the results dropdown based on user interaction

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. Try importing React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Define the sample data array
steps.instruction: Inside the Typeahead component, create a constant array named 'sampleData' containing several fruit names (e.g., 'Apple', 'Banana', 'Cherry') that will be used for autocomplete suggestions.
steps.hint: Declare the array using 'const' inside the component function body, before the return statement. You can include 5-10 fruit names as strings.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a static array of colors
const colors = ['Red', 'Blue', 'Green', 'Yellow'];
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a static dataset ready to be used for filtering suggestions based on user input.
successCriteria: A constant array named 'sampleData' is declared inside the Typeahead component with at least three fruit name strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a sample dataset that will power the autocomplete suggestions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared a constant array with fruit names inside the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sample data array isn't defined correctly. Create a constant array named 'sampleData' with fruit name strings inside the component.

steps.title: Initialize state for the input value
steps.instruction: Inside your Typeahead component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'inputValue' and its setter function, initializing it to an empty string.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty string as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into two variables (e.g., const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState('')).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable for a text input
const [text, setText] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a state variable to track the user's typed input.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty string, and the returned array is destructured into 'inputValue' and 'setInputValue' (or similar names).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to track the user's input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useState with an empty string and destructuring the result into two variables.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the component, use useState to create a state variable for the input value.

steps.title: Initialize state for filtered suggestions
steps.instruction: Inside your Typeahead component, use useState to create a state variable named 'suggestions' and its setter function, initializing it to an empty array.
steps.hint: Add a new useState call that returns an array with two elements: the state variable and its setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for a list
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a 'suggestions' state variable ready to store filtered matches from the items array.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares a 'suggestions' state variable initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to track filtered suggestions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to create a state variable named 'suggestions' initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to add a useState call inside the component to create a 'suggestions' state variable.

steps.title: Create the filter handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your Typeahead component, create a function named handleInputChange that takes an event parameter, updates the inputValue state, and filters the items array to update the suggestions state.
steps.hint: The function should get the current input value from event.target.value, use setInputValue to update state, then filter items to include only those that start with the input value (case-insensitive).
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a handleInputChange function that updates both state variables based on user input.
successCriteria: The handleInputChange function is defined, takes an event parameter, calls setInputValue with event.target.value, and filters items to update suggestions state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the filter handler that will drive the autocomplete behavior.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function updates both inputValue and suggestions states based on the input value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should update inputValue state and filter suggestions. Check that you're using setInputValue and setSuggestions correctly.

steps.title: Create the suggestion selection handler
steps.instruction: Inside your Typeahead component, create a function named handleSuggestionClick that takes a suggestion string as a parameter, sets it as the inputValue, and clears the suggestions array.
steps.hint: The function should call setInputValue with the suggestion and setSuggestions with an empty array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSuggestionClick function is defined that updates inputValue and clears suggestions.
successCriteria: The handleSuggestionClick function is defined, takes a suggestion parameter, calls setInputValue with it, and calls setSuggestions with an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the handler that will update the input and clear suggestions when a user clicks a suggestion.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes a suggestion parameter and updates both inputValue and suggestions state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. It should take a suggestion, set it as inputValue, and clear the suggestions array.

steps.title: Add the input element and wire its onChange
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add an input element with its value bound to the inputValue state and its onChange event wired to call handleInputChange.
steps.hint: Use the input element's value attribute to bind it to inputValue, and set onChange to handleInputChange.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: input element with value binding and onChange
<input value={inputValue} onChange={handleInputChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will be rendered with its value controlled by the inputValue state, and typing will trigger the filter handler.
successCriteria: The input element has value={inputValue} and onChange={handleInputChange} attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The input element is now properly connected to your state and filter handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input element, but make sure it has both value={inputValue} and onChange={handleInputChange} attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or not properly wired. Add an input element with value={inputValue} and onChange={handleInputChange}.

steps.title: Add a container for the suggestions list
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your Typeahead component, add a div element after the input element to serve as the container for the suggestions list.
steps.hint: Add a <div> element right after the closing tag of the input element. This div will eventually hold the list of suggestions.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: adding a container element
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a div element after the input that will later hold the suggestions list.
successCriteria: A div element is added after the input element in the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the container for the suggestions list. This empty div will soon hold the filtered suggestions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div element after the input element inside the return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Add a div element after the input element to create a container for the suggestions list.

steps.title: Map over suggestions to display list items
steps.instruction: Inside the suggestions container, map over the suggestions state array to render each item as a list item (li).
steps.hint: Use the map method on the suggestions array to create an array of JSX elements. Each suggestion should be wrapped in an <li> tag.
steps.expectedOutcome: The suggestions array is mapped to <li> elements, each displaying a suggestion.
successCriteria: The suggestions container contains a map function that returns <li> elements for each suggestion.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped over the suggestions array to display each item as a list element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the map method on the suggestions array and returning an <li> for each item.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to map over the suggestions array to create list items.

steps.title: Wire click events to suggestion items
steps.instruction: Add an onClick handler to each suggestion list item that calls the handleSelect function with the item's text.
steps.hint: Inside the map function where you render each suggestion, add onClick={() => handleSelect(item)} to the <li> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each suggestion list item will be clickable and will call handleSelect when clicked.
successCriteria: The onClick handler is added to each <li> element inside the suggestions map, calling handleSelect with the item's text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully made the suggestion items interactive by adding click handlers.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the onClick handler calls handleSelect with the correct item text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The click handler isn't properly connected. Check that you're adding onClick={() => handleSelect(item)} to each <li> element.

steps.title: Conditionally show the suggestions container
steps.instruction: Wrap the suggestions container in a conditional that only renders it when the suggestions array is not empty.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator or logical AND (&&) to conditionally render the suggestions list based on whether suggestions has items.
steps.expectedOutcome: The suggestions list will only appear when there are matching items, and disappear when the input is cleared or a suggestion is selected.
successCriteria: The suggestions container is wrapped in a conditional that checks if suggestions array has items.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering to show the suggestions only when there are matches.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the conditional might not be checking the suggestions array correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The suggestions list should only appear when there are filtered suggestions. Try using a conditional like `suggestions.length > 0 && (...)`.
